metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Mai 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.131

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Mai 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.131
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.131
- Datum: 05.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, we are missing very much your letters but we
know it is not your fault - there are now terrific gales which sweep
the country and many of the planes have to wait. Here it seems that
the United States are going fast into help for England and finally all
the obstacles are cleared away. But I know you have the heavier part to
bear and you may imagine with what feeling we read about the attacks
on Bristol, so near of your house. At least you have not to worry about
your daughter, it seems that she likes her new house very much - she
writes always we should come to visit her, but unfortunately it is
not so easy as she thinks. We have 1 hour 50 minutes to Newyork, from
there to another station, from there to Croton, from there with a car
to her house and we have no car; it cannot be done in one day.
and Lotte has been ill for ten days, we have lost much time and have
still to go to Baltimore for two days. And we hope to have her here
in Newhaven in April for a few days - we are afraid she will not
know what to do here, as there is nothing except the library and no
distrea at all. We hope however that she will be a little recruited
of you and having opportunity to talk about you abundantly. -
Alltogether we feel very often very sad, - the first war took five
years of my life and this one, a hundred times more violent,
will take all bright and quiet way of living away from us for
years and years. And I shall soon be 60 years old. This living in
Hotels, which we not afeable at all, and in foreign countries be-
comes in the long run very oppressive; just our generation has such
an unlucky time! Some times I wish I had also to pass examinations
or to do some public work; what means literature today against
the dramatic of our daily history! As soon as we have news from
you, you shall hear more from us. In the mean time kindest regards
to all from yours
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief in violetter Tinte. Sehr gut lesbar.
Farbskala/Grauskala fuer Archivierung. Überlagert den Text des Briefes (identisch mit Seite 1).

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr deutlich geschrieben und gut lesbar. Einzig das Wort 'distrea' (Zeile 17) scheint ein Schreibfehler des Autors für 'distractions' oder ähnlich zu sein, wurde aber originalgetreu transkribiert.
